name: where does the comma go
teacher:
Good catch — that's exactly the problem. Your line gives `Hello An`, but the test wants `Hello, An`. The comma is missing.

The comma is not a special symbol here. It is just text. So it must live inside quotes, like the word Hello and the space do.

Now read the expected output slowly: `Hello, An`. After the word Hello comes a comma, then a space, then the name.

Ask yourself: which pieces of my line should hold that comma? Could the comma be inside the same quotes as Hello, or does it get its own pair of quotes? Either way, there are still three pieces joined with `+` — you just need the comma to appear before the space.

Write your `return` line again with that in mind, run `hello("An")`, and tell me what comes out.

Good — the failing test tells you exactly what to fix. The test is the target, not the wording.

Look at what your line produced: `Hello An`. Now look at what it should be: `Hello, An`. The only difference is the comma.

Hint level 1: text you want the function to give back sits between quotes, like `"Hello"`.

name: run output correction
teacher:
Your run output tells you the whole story. You got `Hello An`. The test wants `Hello, An`. The only missing thing is the comma.

Here's hint level 2: you join pieces of text with `+`. Each piece sits in its own quotes. And a space is text too, so it gets its own quotes: `" "`.

That means punctuation is text as well. A comma is not special. It has to live inside quotes, just like the word Hello does.

So look at your first piece. It holds the word Hello. Where would you put the comma so it comes out right after Hello and before the space? Inside those quotes, right after the last letter, before the closing quote. Don't add a space inside that piece — the space is still its own middle piece.

A different example, not your answer: to get `Good, morning`, you'd slip the comma into the first piece before its closing quote, and keep the space as its own piece.

So your line still has three pieces and two `+` signs. Only the first piece changes, by one character.

Make that one small edit. Keep your `#` comment above the `return`. Then run `hello("An")` and tell me what comes out.
